description: Daily account-level metrics aligned to a calendar spine from each account's first event through the current date.

business_logic: '- Reference all calendar dates (date_day) from intermediate.int_pendo__calendar_spine. - Reference daily account metrics from intermediate.int_pendo__account_daily_metrics. - For each account_id present in daily_metrics, compute first_event_on as the minimum occurred_on. - Build an account-specific calendar by pairing each account_id with every date_day such that: - date_day >= first_event_on - date_day <= the current date at execution time (cast(current_timestamp as date), using warehouse/system timezone). - Left join this account-specific calendar to daily_metrics on: - account_id equality - date_day equals occurred_on - Copy metric columns directly from daily_metrics; when no match exists for a given (account_id, date_day), all metric columns are NULL. - No aggregation, de-duplication, or ordering is applied. If daily_metrics contains multiple rows for the same (account_id, occurred_on), the output includes one row per matching source record (duplicating the calendar row). - Accounts with no rows in daily_metrics do not appear in the output.'

business_logic: 'Build a comprehensive customer record per visitor_id by joining base visitor activity with lifecycle, RFM, and product health, then derive journey labels, values, and recommendations: 1) Base rowset and joins - Start from marts.pendo__visitor (vb), one row per visitor_id; carry: visitor_id, account_id, first_event_on, last_event_on, count_active_days, count_active_months, sum_events, sum_minutes, average_daily_events, average_daily_minutes, count_associated_accounts. - Left join intermediate.int_pendo__user_lifecycle_segments (lc) on visitor_id. - Left join intermediate.int_pendo__customer_rfm_analysis (rfm) on visitor_id. - Left join intermediate.int_pendo__product_health_metrics (ph) on account_id. - Null policy: Left joins may yield missing lifecycle/RFM/health attributes; unless explicitly defaulted in rules below, missing values do not match conditions and fall to the default outcome. 2) Customer segmentation label (customer_segment_label) evaluated in order: - Power User + Champions → "Star Customer" - (Mature User or Power User) + High Value → "Key Account" - New User + New Customers → "Fresh Prospect" - Growing User + Potential Loyalists → "Rising Star" - churn_risk_level in (High Risk, Medium Risk) + At Risk → "Save Immediately" - lifecycle_stage = At Risk + action_priority = Re-engagement → "Rescue Mission" - lifecycle_stage = Churned → "Lost Customer" - Else → "Standard Customer" 3) Comprehensive customer value (comprehensive_customer_value, 0–100): - Compute a weighted sum: 40% of user_value_score (defaults to 0 if missing), 30% of (rfm_composite_score scaled to 0–100 by multiplying by 20; defaults to 0 if missing), and 30% of overall_health_score (defaults to 50 if missing). Cap the result at 100. No rounding beyond native numeric evaluation. 4) Recommended next action (recommended_next_action) evaluated in order: - Power User + Champions → "Leverage as advocate; Offer exclusive features; Request testimonials" - is_new_user = true + New Customers → "Intensive onboarding; Feature education; Success manager assignment" - needs_attention = true + action_priority = Re-engagement → "Personalized outreach; Usage analysis; Feature recommendations" - churn_risk_level = High Risk → "Immediate intervention; Executive outreach; Value demonstration" - lifecycle_stage = Growing User → "Feature adoption campaign; Usage optimization; Upgrade path guidance" - rfm_segment = Loyal Customers → "Upsell opportunities; Loyalty rewards; Advanced feature training" - Else → "Standard nurturing; Regular check-ins; Content engagement" 5) Customer journey stage (customer_journey_stage): - Define days since first event as the number of days from the first_event_on date to today. - If days since first event ≤ 30 → "Onboarding" - Else if lifecycle_stage in (Growing User, Mature User) and customer_value_tier in (High Value, Medium Value) → "Growth" - Else if lifecycle_stage in (Power User, Mature User) and rfm_segment in (Champions, Loyal Customers) → "Maturity" - Else if churn_risk_level in (High Risk, Medium Risk) or lifecycle_stage = At Risk → "Retention" - Else if lifecycle_stage = Churned → "Win-back" - Else → "Maintenance" 6) Predicted LTV tier (predicted_ltv_tier) evaluated in order: - lifecycle_stage in (Power User, Mature User) + customer_value_tier = High Value + overall_health_score ≥ 70 (treat missing health as 60 for this rule) → "Very High LTV" - (user_value_score ≥ 70 or rfm_composite_score ≥ 4) + churn_risk_level = Low Risk → "High LTV" - lifecycle_stage in (Growing User, New User) + predicted_clv_tier in (High CLV, Medium CLV) → "Moderate LTV" - churn_risk_level = High Risk or lifecycle_stage = Churned → "Low LTV" - Else → "Standard LTV" 7) Engagement velocity and trends (from comprehensive view): - engagement_velocity: ratio of count_active_days to days since first event; if either value is not positive, set to 0. - usage_trend: define a baseline average as sum_events divided by count_active_days when count_active_days > 0; if average_daily_events exceeds the baseline by more than 20% → "Accelerating"; if within ±20% → "Stable"; otherwise → "Declining". When count_active_days = 0, the baseline is undefined and the outcome is "Declining". - account_influence_level: count_associated_accounts > 3 → "Multi-Account Influencer"; > 1 → "Cross-Account User"; else → "Single Account User". - calculated_at: timestamp when the metrics are computed. 8) Final importance and investment expectation: - customer_importance_level (in order): - customer_segment_label in (Star Customer, Key Account) + predicted_ltv_tier = Very High LTV → "Critical" - comprehensive_customer_value ≥ 80 + customer_journey_stage in (Growth, Maturity) → "High" - comprehensive_customer_value ≥ 60 or customer_segment_label in (Rising Star, Fresh Prospect) → "Medium" - needs_attention = true or customer_journey_stage = Retention → "At Risk" - Else → "Standard" - investment_expectation: - Star Customer → "High ROI - Advocacy & Expansion" - Key Account → "High ROI - Retention & Upsell" - Rising Star → "Medium ROI - Growth Investment" - Fresh Prospect → "Medium ROI - Onboarding Investment" - Save Immediately → "Low ROI - Retention Cost" - Lost Customer → "Negative ROI - Win-back Cost" - Else → "Standard ROI - Maintenance" 9) Output all selected and derived columns; no additional filtering; grain remains one row per visitor_id.'

business_logic: '- Build account_performance_summary: - Source: staging.stg_pendo__account_history left join intermediate.int_pendo__product_health_metrics on account_id. - One row per account with: account_id, account_name set equal to account_id, agent_is_paying=true, agent_planlevel=''Standard'', first_visit=first_visit_at, last_visit=last_visit_at. - Set per-account defaults: critical_customers=0, high_value_customers=0, customers_at_risk=0, onboarding_customers=0, total_active_users=0, avg_customer_value_score=50.0, high_ltv_customers=0. - For each account, derive product metrics as the maximum values across joined product_health rows: product_health_score (overall_health_score), account_nps (net_promoter_score), feature_adoption_rate, and customer_retention_30d. - Derive revenue_health_indicators from account_performance_summary: - revenue_health_status: - If agent_is_paying and avg_customer_value_score ≥ 80 → Excellent; if agent_is_paying and ≥ 60 → Good; if agent_is_paying and < 60 → At Risk. - If not paying and high_ltv_customers > 0 → Conversion Opportunity; otherwise Standard. - account_risk_level (in order): if customers_at_risk / total_active_users > 0.3 → High Risk; else if > 0.15 → Medium Risk; else if product_health_score < 50 → Medium Risk; else if account_nps < 0 → High Risk; otherwise Low Risk. When total_active_users=0, the ratio is treated as NULL and later rules apply. - growth_potential (in order): if high_ltv_customers > (critical_customers + high_value_customers) and feature_adoption_rate > 0.4 → High Growth Potential; else if onboarding_customers > 0 and avg_customer_value_score > 60 → Moderate Growth Potential; else if total_active_users > 10 and customer_retention_30d > 0.7 → Stable Growth; otherwise Limited Growth. - Aggregate platform_wide_kpis across all accounts in revenue_health_indicators: - total_accounts = distinct account count; paying_accounts = distinct account count where agent_is_paying; conversion_rate = paying_accounts / total_accounts (no zero-denominator guard). - platform_total_users = sum(total_active_users); strategic_customers = sum(critical_customers + high_value_customers); customers_needing_attention = sum(customers_at_risk); new_customers_onboarding = sum(onboarding_customers). Sums ignore NULL inputs. - Averages (NULLs ignored): avg_platform_health_score, avg_platform_nps, avg_feature_adoption, avg_retention_rate, avg_customer_value. - Risk/growth counts: number of accounts labeled High/Medium/Low Risk; number with High Growth Potential; number with revenue_health_status = Excellent; number with revenue_health_status = Conversion Opportunity. - calculation_date = current_date at execution. - Compute trend_analysis from staging.stg_pendo__event over the last 30 days (occurred_at within 30 days of now): - For each day, compute: daily_active_accounts (distinct accounts), daily_active_users (distinct users), daily_total_events (sum of events), daily_total_minutes (sum of minutes). - Across these 30 days, compute averages of the daily metrics and user_activity_volatility as the standard deviation of daily_active_users. - user_growth_rate_7d = (average daily_active_users in the last 7 days minus average in the prior 7 days) divided by the prior 7-day average; if the denominator is zero or missing this rate is NULL; expose user_growth_rate_7d with NULL replaced by 0. - growth_trend_assessment is based on the unfilled (raw) user_growth_rate_7d: >0.1 Strong Growth; >0.05 Moderate Growth; >-0.05 Stable; >-0.1 Slight Decline; otherwise Concerning Decline (NULL falls to the final category). - Produce executive_summary_scorecard (final output, single row): - Cross join platform_wide_kpis with trend_analysis. - overall_business_health_score: weighted composite capped at 100 using: - 25% product health score; 15% normalized NPS (NPS shifted from [-1,1] to [0,100]); 15% feature adoption rate scaled to 0–100; 15% retention rate scaled to 0–100; 10% conversion rate scaled to 0–100; 20% growth component where baseline is 50 and adjusted upward by 100×growth when positive, or scaled down by multiplying 50 by (1 + growth) when negative; the growth rate used here is the coalesced value. - primary_alert_status (first match wins): high_risk_accounts > 20% of total_accounts → Account Risk Alert; avg_platform_nps < -0.2 → Customer Satisfaction Alert; user_growth_rate_7d < -0.1 → Growth Decline Alert; avg_retention_rate < 0.6 → Retention Alert; customers_needing_attention > 25% of platform_total_users → Customer Health Alert; otherwise All Systems Normal. - strategic_recommendation (first match wins): conversion_opportunities > 10% of paying_accounts → Focus on conversion optimization; high_growth_accounts > 20% of total_accounts → Capitalize on growth opportunities; customers_needing_attention > strategic_customers → Prioritize customer success initiatives; user_growth_rate_7d < 0 → Address user acquisition and retention; otherwise Maintain current strategy with incremental improvements. - generated_at = current_timestamp at execution.'

WITH f AS (SELECT feature_id,feature_name,group_id,product_area_name,page_id,page_name,CAST(created_at AS DATE) created_on,coalesce(CAST(valid_through AS DATE),current_date) valid_on FROM intermediate.int_pendo__feature_info) SELECT c.date_day,f.feature_id,f.feature_name,f.group_id,f.product_area_name,f.page_id,f.page_name,coalesce(m.sum_clicks,0) sum_clicks,coalesce(m.count_visitors,0) count_visitors,coalesce(m.count_accounts,0) count_accounts,coalesce(m.count_first_time_visitors,0) count_first_time_visitors,coalesce(m.count_first_time_accounts,0) count_first_time_accounts,coalesce(m.count_return_visitors,0) count_return_visitors,coalesce(m.count_return_accounts,0) count_return_accounts,coalesce(m.avg_daily_minutes_per_visitor,0) avg_daily_minutes_per_visitor,coalesce(m.avg_daily_clicks_per_visitor,0) avg_daily_clicks_per_visitor,coalesce(m.percent_of_daily_feature_clicks,0) percent_of_daily_feature_clicks,coalesce(m.percent_of_daily_feature_visitors,0) percent_of_daily_feature_visitors,coalesce(m.percent_of_daily_feature_accounts,0) percent_of_daily_feature_accounts,coalesce(m.count_click_events,0) count_click_events FROM f CROSS JOIN intermediate.int_pendo__calendar_spine c LEFT JOIN intermediate.int_pendo__feature_daily_metrics m ON m.feature_id=f.feature_id AND m.occurred_on=c.date_day WHERE c.date_day BETWEEN f.created_on AND f.valid_on

business_logic: '- Build a daily date spine from intermediate.int_pendo__calendar_spine using date_day. - From intermediate.int_pendo__feature_info, derive created_on as the calendar date of created_at and valid_through_date as the calendar date of valid_through; if valid_through is blank, use the current date.
